rules: Latest stable only. No prerelease, no release candidate, no git dependency in a release build.
Every version was read from crates.io or the Rust release channel at generatedAt. None came from memory.
A major jump is a reviewed decision with a migration note. The `windows` crate moves fast and a major bump can rename types across every FFI call site (REQ-VER-04).
In a Rust binary every dependency is compiled into the shipped product, so adding one is a shipping decision, not a development convenience (REQ-SBM-05).
Re-validate at gate H2. A manifest older than staleAfterDays fails the gate.
crates.io requires a User-Agent header. A request without one is rejected, which is easy to misread as 'crate not found'.

rust.note: Pinned in rust-toolchain.toml so every build and CI run uses one compiler (REQ-FND-02). The MSRV is stated separately and tested (REQ-VER-06).

windows.note: The only route to Win32/WinRT (REQ-FND-03). Used exclusively inside crates/ffi (contracts/ownership.md). Pair the version with windows-sys deliberately - a mismatched pair compiles and then disagrees about type layout (REQ-VER-05).

windows-sys.note: Raw bindings. Prefer `windows` unless a call is missing from it.

windows-registry.note: Registry access for the autostart entry and ARP registration. B08 and B07 only.

windows-service.note: Service lifecycle (REQ-SVC-01..05). B08 only; nobody shells out to sc.exe (contracts/ownership.md).

eframe.note: Default UI framework. Chosen because the design tokens are plain Rust values, which makes REQ-MOC-02's compiled mockups trivially achievable and REQ-DSN-02's 'tokens are code' literal. It is not a native-look framework - that is the tradeoff, and it is an intake decision (REQ-UI-01).

egui.note: Must match eframe's minor exactly. A mismatch is a confusing trait-resolution error, not a clear one.

iced.note: Intake alternative. Elm-style, themeable; more ceremony, more native feel.

slint.note: Intake alternative. Declarative with its own styling language - a better fit if the design system should live outside Rust, a worse fit for REQ-MOC-02.

tray-icon.note: Tray icon and its Explorer-restart re-registration (REQ-TRY-01, REQ-TRY-02). B06 only.

muda.note: Native menus for the tray context menu (REQ-TRY-04).

rfd.note: Native file dialogs, used by the support bundle (REQ-OBS-04).

self-replace.note: Atomic self-replacement for the update swap (REQ-UPD-06). Verify the signature BEFORE calling it, never after.

self_update.note: Optional convenience over the update flow. Its defaults do not satisfy REQ-UPD-02 - signature verification is ours to add, not its to provide. Record the decision if it is used at all.

minisign-verify.note: Verification only, with the public key embedded (REQ-UPD-03). A verify-only crate is the right dependency here: the binary never needs to sign.

semver.note: Version comparison, including the downgrade refusal (REQ-UPD-05).

cargo-wix.note: MSI for enterprise deployment (REQ-INST-03). A build-time tool, not a dependency.

winres.note: Embeds the application manifest, icon and version resource. The manifest is asInvoker (REQ-FND-11).

cargo-auditable.note: Embeds the dependency list in the shipped binary (REQ-SBM-02). This is the requirement's whole point: an artefact found on a machine can be audited without the release page.

cargo-deny.note: Licence, advisory and duplicate-version gate (REQ-SBM-07). B16 must resolve the exact version at H2 - it was not read in this pass, so it is recorded as unresolved rather than guessed.

tokio.note: Off-UI-thread work (REQ-UI-06). Enable only the features used; the full feature set compiles a great deal into the binary.

anyhow.note: Application error plumbing. Not in the contract crate's public API.

thiserror.note: Typed errors for the contract surface.

keyring.note: Credential-store access for secrets at rest (REQ-SEC-03).

ureq.note: Update fetch. Small and blocking - suits a background task and keeps the dependency tree short. reqwest 0.13.5 is the intake alternative when async HTTP is already present.

sha2.note: Artefact hash check against the signed manifest (REQ-UPD-04).

directories.note: Per-user paths. B01 publishes `paths`; no other crate resolves a directory itself (REQ-SEC-05).

telemetry.note: Asserted by test, not assumed. B11 owns the assertion, and it covers build-time network access by any crate as well as runtime.
checks: no crate performs network I/O in a build script
no runtime HTTP destination outside the configured update endpoint
